title: Appointment booking — example architecture
status: Illustrative design; targets and hypotheses are unverified

sources.label: Illustrative appointment-system brief
sources.note: Example authored for skill testing; no production observation or benchmark.

boards.title: System responsibilities
boards.subtitle: Logical boundaries may share a deployment; booking correctness is the central constraint.

boards.title: Quality, cause and change
boards.subtitle: Make targets falsifiable and compare a local fix with a shared-boundary repair.

nodes.title: Customer interface
lines: Show available slots and booking status
Retry a request with the same request key
invariants: A timeout is an uncertain result, not proof of booking failure.

nodes.title: Booking boundary
nodes.detail: Keep admission and receipt behavior coherent so retry handling stays local.
invariants: One active reservation per slot; one result per caller request key.

nodes.title: Reservation ledger
lines: Atomic uniqueness of the occupied slot
Persist booking result and caller key
nodes.detail: A relational transaction is a candidate mechanism; actual engine and isolation behavior need verification.

nodes.title: Booking quality scenario
lines: Choose latency/resource limits from measured baseline
nodes.detail: Track success, conflict and timeout paths; include reads and cancellation in regression checks.

nodes.title: Timeout mechanism
nodes.detail: Compare per-stage timings and lock waits against network delay; do not infer cause from one slow endpoint.

nodes.title: Smallest sufficient repair
lines: Local query repair if one query is responsible
Shared ledger repair if multiple consumers contend
New service only for a demonstrated boundary need

nodes.title: Likely change and understanding
lines: Add recurring appointments without leaking storage details
Have an unfamiliar developer trace a retry
Check unaffected search and cancellation paths

edges.label: request / receipt
edges.note: Authenticated caller identity and retry key must reach the booking boundary.
